title: Routing in Express
description: Learn how to define and manage routes in Express.js to handle different HTTP requests, enabling your application to respond dynamically to various endpoints.

lessons.title: What is Routing?
lessons.content: Routing is the process of defining endpoints (URLs) in your web application and specifying how your app should respond to client requests to those endpoints. Each route can handle different HTTP methods like GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, etc., allowing the server to provide different functionalities depending on the request type and path.

lessons.title: Basic Route Handling in Express
Handling Different HTTP Methods
lessons.content:
HTTP defines several methods used to communicate intent to the server:
- **GET:** Retrieve data from the server.
- **POST:** Submit data to the server, often used for form submissions.
- **PUT:** Update existing resources.
- **DELETE:** Remove resources.
Express allows you to handle each method separately for the same URL path.

lessons.title: Route Parameters
Query Strings in Routes
lessons.content: Query strings are key-value pairs appended to URLs after a question mark (e.g., `/search?term=nodejs&sort=asc`). You can access them in Express using `req.query`. This is useful for filtering or searching data without modifying the URL path.

lessons.title: Organizing Routes Using Express Router
lessons.content: As your application grows, managing all routes in a single file becomes difficult. Express provides `express.Router()` to create modular route handlers. You can group related routes in separate files and import them into your main app. This improves code organization and maintainability.

lessons.title: Example of Express Router
Handling 404 - Not Found Routes
lessons.content: When a client requests a route that doesn’t exist, it’s important to handle it gracefully. Express allows you to define a catch-all route placed at the end of your routing setup to send a 404 status and message, improving user experience.
